Ten cases in tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py fail inside a worker's suite run. They are listed as FAILED lines in /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260930T154556201330-a-review-promotes-what-it-passed/suite-head.log. In each, the hook subprocess exits 0 with empty output and the test hits JSONDecodeError. _claude_pid() in reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py resolves the harness from an inherited CLAUDE_PID, or else from the nearest ancestor process whose executable is claude, so a test run under a real harness finds that harness rather than the fixture's session.
First, reproduce at the base: run the file with CLAUDE_PID set to an unrelated live pid in the environment, and show the same failures in a log. Then make every case name its harness identity explicitly, so none reads the inherited CLAUDE_PID or the real ancestry. Set CLAUDE_PID in each subprocess's environment to the pid the fixture registers, or clear it and inject the identity the way the hook allows. Change reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py only if the tests cannot pin the identity without it, and never change what the hook does under a real harness.
Show the file passing in three conditions: under that inherited CLAUDE_PID, with no CLAUDE_PID set, and in a plain run. Log each separately, with first line `revision: <full sha>`. Also give one base log and one head log over tests/test_coordinator_obligations_hook.py tests/test_hook_installer.py tests/test_hooks_install_cli.py, showing zero added failures by id. Use the absolute venv python and a neutral /tmp basetemp you delete afterwards.
